Restore a journal from a backup, or move your journal to a new machine. Bundles from older versions that carry legacyMap still import. Gournal ignores that key.

:::caution
An import can add to or change the entries that you have. Make a backup first. Read the [backups guide](/docs/guides/data-safety-and-backups/).
:::

## CLI: gournal import

Load entries from a bundle file. Make the bundle with gournal export --format bundle.

```text
gournal import <file>
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `<file>` | yes | Path of the bundle file. |

## Examples

### CLI

Make a bundle file, then load it into another journal. Set `GOURNAL_HOME` to the folder of the other journal. This example imports into an empty journal.

```console
$ gournal export -f bundle -o backup.json
✓ Exported 8 entries to backup.json

$ GOURNAL_HOME=~/other-journal gournal import backup.json
Imported: 8 new, 0 updated, 0 unchanged, 0 duplicates merged.
```

Import the same file again into that journal. Gournal finds the same entries and changes nothing.

```console
$ GOURNAL_HOME=~/other-journal gournal import backup.json
Imported: 0 new, 0 updated, 8 unchanged, 0 duplicates merged.
```
